Prevention: Control grassy weeds as they are egg laying sites of armyworms.
Plant trees as barriers around fields to divert armyworm moths.
Deep plough after harvest to expose in-soil hibernating pupae.
Rotate maize with non-cereals, such as legumes.

The management of armyworm is based on early detection.
Young tiny less than 1 cm dull white to greenish caterpillars with orange head only cause small holes in leaves.
If about 1 to 3 small larvae are found per 10 plants consider control action.
Older up to 3 cm light brown caterpillars with narrow white dorsal line eat large areas of leave edges, leaving leaf blades, or eat up entire leaves.
Direct control is then often too late.
